# Build: dispatcher-gate-never-launch-build

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-13T20:07:27.626Z
> what's up with the parallel build that breaks a build up to run on multiple sessions

## What to build
Continue build "Dispatcher gate: never launch a build that already has a live session" (dispatcher-gate-never-launch-build) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-13 20:07):
"what's up with the parallel build that breaks a build up to run on multiple sessions"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Branch: claude/dispatcher-gate-never-launch-build
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~30 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Bug seen three times on Nov 13 (ui-manager-floating-window-to-select-any: Earl/Gina, Gina/Paulie, Lenny/Paulie): the orchestrator's dispatcher launched the same build phase twice on the same worktree, so two headless sessions wrote the same files at once. Also 'Self-check: marked running with no session' releases builds back to the Queue while a session is still alive. Fix: (1) a dispatch gate that refuses a launch while ANY live tmux/claude session exists for that build id or worktree (check tmux axf-<build>--*, claude -p pids and a lock file in the worktree); (2) the self-check must confirm a session is really dead (pid + tmux) before releasing; (3) a per-build lock file with heartbeat, where stale locks expire; (4) tests that simulate double dispatch. This must land BEFORE parallel split (orchestrator-settings-collapsible-split) goes live, since parallel sub-builds must each get their own worktree and branch and never share one.
[ ] s2 (~10 min) what's up with the parallel build that breaks a build up to run on multiple sessions
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/dispatcher-gate-never-launch-build.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/dispatcher-gate-never-launch-build.md, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step dispatcher-gate-never-launch-build <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link dispatcher-gate-never-launch-build --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step dispatcher-gate-never-launch-build <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note dispatcher-gate-never-launch-build "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

open: No Kotlin twin needed: host-side dispatcher tooling only.

The lock heartbeat comes from the dispatcher tick (every minute while the session is alive), not from the session itself. A launch that waits in the agent-slots queue for more than 20 min before tmux starts has an expired lock, but by then the slot entry holds the build (the reaper skips builds whose slot is held).
